about: Errors arc (and the tools it calls) really print, each with where the words come from, what it means and the fix. diagnose.py matches `pattern` (a Python regex) against a command's stdout+stderr. A fix that touches a global file (~/.tars, ~/.arc, ~/.claude) or anything remote is asked first.

issues.source: git's own message, surfaced by arc (crates/apps/cli/src/cli/dispatch.rs require_git_repo)
issues.cause: arc ran outside a git work tree.
issues.fix: cd into the project, or `git init` it if the person agrees.

issues.pattern: (command not found: arc|arc: command not found|No such file or directory: 'arc')
issues.cause: arc is not installed, or its directory is not on PATH.
issues.fix: stage `binary`: install from getarc, or add the directory holding arc to PATH.

issues.source: clap, when the installed arc predates the verb
issues.cause: the installed arc is older than this route: the verb was added later (getarc's newest release may predate it).
issues.fix: compare `arc --version` with the release page; if getarc has nothing newer, stop and say so — do not fake the verb with another.

issues.source: scripts/fetch_arc.py (GitHub's download URL for a tag or asset that does not exist)
issues.cause: the tag is not published on getarc (yet), or it has no asset for this platform.
issues.fix: check the tag with the person and the release page; do not fall back to another tag without saying so.

issues.pattern: no providers found in your tars registry
issues.cause: the tars config has no [providers.<id>] (or arc read a different tars home than you think).
issues.fix: stage `tars`: define one provider in <tars home>/config.toml (ask before writing that global file); pass the same --tars_home to every arc call.

issues.cause: the tars config file could not be read or parsed; the rest of the line is tars's own reason (an unknown key in a provider table is refused: tars-config providers.rs deny_unknown_fields).
issues.fix: show the person the rest of the line; fix the named key in the tars config with their consent.

issues.pattern: missing credential: env var `([A-Za-z0-9_]+)` is not set
issues.cause: the provider reads its key from an environment variable that is not set in the shell arc runs in.
issues.fix: the person exports it themselves (shell profile or `source .env`). Never ask for the key's value, never write it to .arc/.

issues.pattern: arc init needs an interactive terminal
issues.cause: expected when an agent runs `arc init`: stdin is not a terminal, so arc left .arc/config.toml.example instead of asking.
issues.fix: ask the person for the critic and fixer provider ids, copy the example to .arc/config.toml and fill [roles] with them (the example's own instruction).

issues.cause: .arc/config.toml is already there; arc init does not overwrite it.
issues.fix: probe the stage: if [roles] already resolve, the stage is done. Overwrite only if the person asks.

issues.cause: an old-shape .arc/config.toml still defines providers; arc reads providers only from tars.
issues.fix: move each [providers.<id>] to the tars config (ask first — global file), then delete the section from .arc/config.toml.

issues.cause: [roles] has neither that role nor `default`.
issues.fix: add `<role> = "<tars provider id>"` (or `default`) under [roles].

issues.cause: the fixer never falls back to `default`.
issues.fix: add `fixer = "<tars provider id>"`, a different model family from the critic.

issues.cause: a [roles] value names an id the tars config does not define (often: arc read another tars home).
issues.fix: use one of the listed ids, or define that provider in tars; pass the same --tars_home everywhere.

issues.pattern: fixer pipeline: failed to build provider '([^']+)' from config at
issues.cause: the fixer's id is not in the tars config, or that entry does not parse; the rest of the line is tars's words.
issues.fix: fix the tars entry the line names.

issues.cause: a step holds `${{ … }}`; arc runs no expressions, and a merge gate with one refuses every PR.
issues.fix: rewrite with shell variables (`$NODE_ENV`, an `env:` value) and re-run `arc workflow … --list`.

issues.cause: a `uses:` arc does not read (only checkout, setup-node/python/go and dtolnay/rust-toolchain are read, as machine checks).
issues.fix: replace it with plain `run:` steps; the tool it installed must already be on the merge machine.

issues.pattern: no job named (\S+); the file defines:
issues.cause: --job names a job the file does not have.
issues.fix: use one of the jobs the line lists.

issues.cause: arc names the repo from `origin`; this clone has none.
issues.fix: the person adds the GitHub remote (creating a remote repo is an outward action — ask).

issues.cause: `arc local-review` / `arc fix` work through a review service that serves this repo from this machine's ~/.arc/machine.toml. Nothing serves it here. The review service is not publicly released.
issues.fix: not fixable by the install: report it. Registering a tenant is the operator's (`arc-server tenant add`), on a machine running arc's services.

issues.pattern: post-commit-gate (\S+): could not decide, so no review — (.*)
issues.source: crates/apps/cli/src/cli/local_review_dispatch.rs:148 (the post-commit hook prints it to the terminal and .arc/critic.log since #3412); docs/user-guide/coding-agents.md
issues.cause: the post-commit hook asked whether to review this commit and could not decide, so it reviewed nothing. The reason follows the dash — most often the branch has no PR yet (`review.db holds no PR from <branch>: run `arc review` first`) or no review service serves the repo here (`… is not a tenant in …machine.toml`).
issues.fix: read the reason after the dash and follow its own row (no_pr_on_record / not_a_tenant). The commit itself succeeded; nothing to undo.

issues.pattern: review\.db holds no PR from (\S+): run `arc review` first
issues.cause: local-review / fix work on the branch's PR, and this branch has none on record.
issues.fix: `arc review` opens it — an outward action (push + PR): ask first.

issues.pattern: the review service did not take it in
issues.cause: the request was queued but no review service took it within the wait.
issues.fix: report it with the row and request id; the service is the operator's.

issues.pattern: the checkout is on no branch
issues.cause: HEAD is detached; a PR belongs to a branch.
issues.fix: check out a branch (ask before creating one).

issues.cause: ~/.arc/client.toml names no board. The bridge server is an operator's, not publicly released.
issues.fix: only with an address from the operator: write `web = "http://<host>:<port>"` to ~/.arc/client.toml (ask first — global file).
